title: Import penetration and manufacturing employment: evidence from Africa
summary: Cross-country evidence on the labour market effects of import penetration in Africa is scarce. This paper studies how imports of intermediate and final goods affect manufacturing employment across African countries.
keyFindings: Intermediate-good import penetration raises manufacturing employment, while final-good import penetration has a negative or, at best, insignificant effect.
Intermediate imports from developed countries increase employment, while those from developing countries reduce it.
methods: Manufacturing industry and establishment-level data from 20 African countries.
